label: Water buffalo

sources.text: The article gives the domestic form as Bubalus bubalis, and says the ICZN's March 2003 ruling kept B. bubalis valid for the domestic form.

about.text: Water buffalo are domesticated bovines kept for milk, work and meat, in two types: the river buffalo, kept mainly for milk and transport, and the swamp buffalo, kept mainly for work. Most are in Asia, and India and Pakistan are the largest milk producers.

links.name: FAO: Gateway to dairy production and products, buffaloes

sources.text: The two types and their uses are from the Wikipedia article as fetched. India and Pakistan as the largest milk producers, and the milk-and-work uses, are from the FAO gateway page, which gives no year.

domestication.where: Western India (river type) and mainland Southeast Asia (swamp type), two separate domestications
domestication.text: The river type was probably domesticated about 6,300 years ago in western India, and the swamp type was domesticated separately 3,000 to 7,000 years ago in mainland Southeast Asia.

sources.text: Places and dates from the article's river and swamp type sections. The country list for mainland Southeast Asia is my own mapping of that region to today's countries, not from the article.

Wikipedia's 208 million (2020) and 72 million tonnes of milk (no year) differ from FAOSTAT's 2023 figures, so FAOSTAT's figures were used.
